# Benchmark: scrub a stored reply before cutting it to 200 characters
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #92, sha256:6d7c5ccbfc1c5db203710a88b652e2f37cdcb559881350e556a2d643ac45653d). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Done 2026-10-27 (233fac5: scrub before the cut, tilde paths masked, history scanner; clean; review Copilot Yes, Grok sound (D44))
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** bug (thin slice; a benchmark change needs its own Decider and old rows stay labeled)
- **Milestone:** Measure first: does Phrase beat plain C# on tokens and attempts?
- **Source:** Thin-slice rule (Decider D18) applied to old card 037 (it bundled six criteria and a harness defect), under the agile ruling (VISION ruling 6), while Steve's measure-first priority (Decider D31) needs the docs-in-context mode for the Phrase arm of the head-to-head. Sliced by the facilitator and PM 2026-10-27; any seat may challenge it.
- **Depends on:** 085
- **Story:** As Morgan, I want the stored reply head to be scrubbed first and cut second, with home-relative paths masked too, so that I can read a published benchmark row without a path or a name leaking into a public file.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given a reply containing a user path that is replaced by a placeholder, When the head is stored, Then the scrub runs before the cut, so a head never exceeds 200 characters after replacement
  2. Given a reply containing a home-relative path (a tilde followed by AppData), When the head is stored, Then that path is masked as well
  3. Given the stored history rows, When they are scanned, Then none contains a path or a user name (the three rows fixed by hand stay as they are)
